main_text.p: coronatos ἐφοδίῳ[?] gratia secum sumturū. Addit se illibenter alibi, quàm in ea urbe, in qua percommodè annis aliquot uixis-set, actūrum[?]. Quid multis? Bona parte pecunię penes Patremfamiliâs depofita, & spe reditus facta, iter ingreditur. Erat perquàm incommodum Patrifamiliâs, eo te poris articulo hominem dimittere[?]. Sed humanitati id dandum uidebatur. Nec multo post redux, reliquam pecuniam penes eundem deponit, nonnulla de facultatibus paternis aperit: & tandem tinnulis iftis rationibus perficit, ut gener factus, socero demortuo succederet. Quòd autem honesti esset illius mores, ad Senatoriam dignitate euectus, diuq; ea sic functus est, ut haberetur ἀνέγκλητος[?]. Sed tandem malae conscientiae doloribus sic excruciatus est, ut homo αὐτοκατάκριτος[?] mori mallet, quàm diutiùs in tantis uersari angustijs. Die quadam praefituta iudicio capitali, homicidae cuiusdam nomine, quòd ipse quoq; è iudicum numero esset, iussus est adesse. page.notes: Greek words are printed in italic and their letters are hard to read at this scan size; the accents and breathings are uncertain, so all Greek is marked [?]. "actūrum" (ct ligature) and "summo" (the word is split across lines without a hyphen) are doubtful. "eo te / poris" appears split without a printed hyphen; the full word is uncertain. The faint marks at the lower left are edge shadow and the stains at the bottom are not printing, so they are left out.
